To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dichlorocarbenezinc chloride functionalized SWCNTs exhibit semiconducting to metallic transition.

the electrical properties of m- and s- SWCNTs are significantly affected by carbene-based co-valent functionalization, and the transition from semiconducting to metallic state upon dichlorocar-bene functionalization is reversible upon thermal treatment.

the electrical conductivity of m-SWCnt is unaffected by carbene functionalization, whereas the electrical conductivity of semiconducting SWCNTs decreases by a factor of 10, and the conductivity of a mixture of m- and s-CNTs is reduced by a factor of two.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new methods for the functionalization of single-walled carbon nanostructures, with particular attention to the effects of functionalization on the electronic and magnetic properties of these systems.
the synthesis and characterization of functionalized SWCNTs, and with the study of the effects of covalent functional groups on the electrical properties and the structure of SWCNTs.
the development and characterization of new materials based on single-walled carbon nano-tubes (SWCNTs) and graphene, and their application in nanoscale electronic devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dichlorocarbenezation of SWCNTs can be used to selectively functionalize s-SWCNT networks without significantly affecting the properties of m-SWNTs.
the electrical properties of m- and s- SWCNTs are not significantly affected upon dichlorocarbenefunctionalization.
the carbene-based functionalization process is a promising approach for the selective modification of SWCNTs and the fabrication of SWCNT-based electronic devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an approach for the selective functionalization of semiconducting SWCNTs.
the dichlorocarbenezinc chloride (DCCZnCl2) functionalized m-SWCNT has a high conductivity and a low resistance, while the s-SWCNT shows a low conductivity and a high resistance.
carbene functionalization of SWCNTs is a promising method to selectively modify semiconducting SWCNTs, and to transform semiconducting into metallic ones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
carbene-functionalization of SWCNTs can be a useful tool for sorting metallic from semiconducting SWCNTs, and for tuning the electrical properties of SWCNT networks.
the electrical properties of m- and s-carbene-SWCNTs can be tailored for different applications.
carbene functionalization is a promising technique for the separation of m- and s- SWCNTs.
